Greetings, goodbyes and titles · 8 min

Formal or informal?

We change our expressions depending on who we talk to: a professor, the dean, or a classmate.

SituationFormalInformal
GreetingGood morning / afternoon / evening, Professor García.Hi! / Hello!
Meeting someonePleased to meet you.Nice to meet you!
Saying goodbyeGoodbye. Have a nice day.Bye! / See you later!
Saying thanksThank you very much.Thanks!
TitleUsed forExample
Professor / Prof.a university teacherGood morning, Professor García.
Dr.a person with a doctorateThis is Dr. López.
Mr.a manMr. Fernández, the secretary.
Ms. / Mrs.a womanMs. Rodríguez, from the administration.

Adverbs of frequency

How often?

AdverbHow often (%)
always100%
usually~90%
often~70%
sometimes~50%
rarely~10%
never0%
Before the main verbShe always studies at night.
After the verb to beShe is often tired.
Expressions go at the endI check my email every day.
every dayonce a weektwice a monthon Mondayson weekends

Articles, nouns, plurals, adjectives · 15 min

Articles and nouns

a / an

Indefinite

  • a before a consonant sound: a student, a university
  • an before a vowel sound: an engineer, an hour
the

Definite

  • a specific or unique thing: the library, the UK
Aa

Proper nouns

  • Names of people, countries, nationalities, languages, days: Lucía, Argentina, Spanish, Monday
  • Common nouns (student, city) have no capital letter.
+s

Plurals

  • +s: student → students
  • +es: box → boxes, watch → watches
  • y → ies: city → cities
  • irregular: woman → women, child → children

1Complete with a, an or the.

Adjectives and possessives

😊

Descriptive adjectives

  • tall / short · young / old
  • friendly · shy · funny
  • hard-working · intelligent
  • They go before a noun and never take -s: a friendly teacher, friendly teachers.
my

Possessive adjectives

  • I → my · you → your
  • he → his · she → her · it → its
  • we → our · they → their
  • One owner: Lucía's advisor

You are a good student. ____ notes are very clear.

5Choose the correct form.

Lucía is ____ student.
The lecturers are very ____.

Reading · 12 min

Meet Julia

Hello! My name is Julia Fernández. I'm twenty years old and I'm from Mendoza, Argentina. I live in Santa Rosa now because I study Geography at university. I'm a first-year student. I have classes from Monday to Thursday and I study in person on campus, but on Fridays I always study online. My classmates are friendly and my professor, Dr. Salas, is very kind. I speak Spanish and a little English. I like music and films, and my favourite activity is travelling with my friends. In my free time, I usually read.

My best friend is Tomás. He's an exchange student from Chile, and his language is Spanish too.

1True or false?

Julia is from Santa Rosa.
She studies Geography.
Dr. Salas is her classmate.
Tomás is from Chile.
Julia speaks Spanish and a little English.
Julia is a second-year student.
On Fridays, Julia studies online.

2Answer the questions.

What does she like?
When does Julia study online?

Everybody lives in Santa Rosa.

  1. Meet informally

    Greet your classmate, introduce yourself and ask four questions about their card.

  2. Spell it

    Ask "How do you spell your surname?" and write it down.

  3. Introduce formally

    Introduce your partner to a professor: "Good morning, Professor ___. This is ___. He/She is from ___ and he/she studies ___."

  4. Say goodbye

    Close the conversation in a formal and then in an informal way. Switch roles.

Hi! I'm... Where are you from? What do you study? What's your surname? Good morning, Professor... This is... He's / She's from... Pleased to meet you. Goodbye. Have a nice day. See you later!

Writing · 8 min

An email to a professor

Write a short formal email to a new professor. Introduce yourself (name, age, where you are from, where you live, what you study) and use a formal greeting and closing.

Dear Professor…,
My name is…
I'm … years old.
I'm from…
I live in…
I study…
I'm a … year student.
Thank you very much.
Best regards,
See a model email

Dear Professor García,
My name is Camila Rocha. I'm twenty years old and I'm from Brazil. I live in Santa Rosa and I study Nursing. I'm a first-year student. I speak Portuguese and Spanish. Thank you very much.
Best regards,
Camila Rocha

0 words

Before you finish, check:

  • I used Dear + a title
  • I wrote my name, age and where I'm from
  • I wrote where I live and what I study
  • I used am / is / are correctly
  • I used the Simple Present correctly
  • I said thank you and used a formal closing
